{"type":"tool_result","timestamp":"2026-11-15T16:08:16.884Z","tool_id":"run_shell_command__call_8816476904281030069","status":"success","output":"/**\n * declare-near-use — declare variables close to their usage. A `const` bound\n * at the top of a block and first read a dozen statements later makes the\n * reader carry it the whole way down; declaring it right above its first use\n * keeps the value and its purpose on the same screen.\n *\n * What counts: a `const` / `let` declaration that is a direct child of a\n * `BlockStatement` or `Program`, whose first reference (init reference\n * excluded) lands in a sibling statement of the same list. When more than\n * `maxDistance` (default 5) statements separate the declaration from that\n * sibling, the declaration is reported. Skipped, because a later position\n * would change meaning or is not obviously better:\n *   - the first reference sits inside a nested block or function (a loop body,\n *     a callback, an `if` arm) — hoisting it into the branch is a judgment call;\n *   - references spread over two or more branching siblings (`if` / `switch` /\n *     `try`) — the declaration is shared state between arms;\n *   - `let` without an initialiser — deliberately declared for later assignment;\n *   - `var`, and exported Program-level declarations (an export is a reference).\n *\n * Detect-only: moving a declaration past side-effecting statements needs a\n * human to confirm nothing observes the old order.\n */\nconst BLOCK_PARENTS = new Set([\"BlockStatement\", \"Program\"]);\nconst BRANCHING = new Set([\"IfStatement\", \"SwitchStatement\", \"TryStatement\"]);\nconst NESTING = new Set([\n    \"BlockStatement\",\n    \"FunctionDeclaration\",\n    \"FunctionExpression\",\n    \"ArrowFunctionExpression\",\n    \"ClassBody\",\n    \"StaticBlock\",\n]);\nfunction isCandidate(node) {\n    if (node.kind === \"var\" || !BLOCK_PARENTS.has(node.parent.type)) {\n        return false;\n    }\n    return node.declarations.every((declarator) => declarator.init);\n}\n/**\n * Walks from a reference up to the statement list holding `declaration`,\n * noting whether a nested scope sits between the reference and that sibling.\n */\nfunction locateReference(identifier, declaration) {\n    const list = declaration.parent;\n    let node = identifier;\n    let nested = false;\n    while (node.parent && node.parent !== list) {\n        node = node.parent;\n        nested = nested || NESTING.has(node.type);\n    }\n---\n/**\n * max-expects — one assertion per test. A test that checks five fields with\n * five `expect` calls stops at the first failure and hides the other four;\n * `expect(result).toEqual({...})` shows the whole diff at once, and a test\n * that genuinely needs two unrelated assertions is two tests.\n *\n * What counts: inside the callback of `it(...)` / `test(...)` and their\n * `.only` / `.skip` / `.each(...)` forms, every `expect(...)` call — the\n * ROOT call, so `expect(x).resolves.toEqual(y)` is one, not three.\n * `expect.assertions(n)` and `expect.hasAssertions()` are bookkeeping, not\n * assertions, and are not counted. Helper functions declared inside the test\n * body count toward the test that contains them: hiding assertions in a local\n * closure does not make the test smaller.\n *\n * Reported at the test call. Detect-only: which assertions merge into one\n * object and which become their own test is the author's call.\n */\nconst TEST_ROOTS = new Set([\"it\", \"test\"]);\nconst TEST_MODIFIERS = new Set([\"only\", \"skip\", \"each\", \"concurrent\"]);\nfunction isTestRoot(node) {\n    return node.type === \"Identifier\" && TEST_ROOTS.has(node.name);\n}\nfunction isTestModifier(node) {\n    return (node.type === \"MemberExpression\" &&\n        !node.computed &&\n        isTestRoot(node.object) &&\n        TEST_MODIFIERS.has(node.property.name));\n}\nfunction isTestCall(node) {\n    const { callee } = node;\n    if (isTestRoot(callee) || isTestModifier(callee)) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // it.each(table)(\"name\", fn) — the callee is itself the `it.each(...)` call\n    return callee.type === \"CallExpression\" && isTestModifier(callee.callee);\n}\nfunction isExpectRootCall(node) {\n    return node.callee.type === \"Identifier\" && node.callee.name === \"expect\";\n}\nexport default {\n---\n/**\n * callee-below-caller — place functions in the downward direction: a reader\n * meets the caller first and finds the callee below it. A file then reads like\n * a newspaper — headline at the top, detail as you scroll — instead of forcing\n * the reader to hold a pile of helpers in their head before the point arrives.\n *\n * What counts: only top-level `FunctionDeclaration`s (direct `Program` children,\n * including `export function`). For each, the FIRST reference in source order\n * that lives inside another top-level function names its caller; a callee whose\n * declaration sits ABOVE that caller is reported. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":"2026-11-15T16:09:17.030Z","tool_name":"replace","tool_id":"replace__call_411725369257196873","parameters":{"new_string":"    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n    if (!tool) {\n      log.warn('tool', 'tool not found', {name});\n      throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}`);\n    }\n    const validator = tool.validator ?? resolveDynamicValidator(this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource));\n    if (!validator(input)) {\n      log.warn('tool', 'input validation failed', {name});\n      return {result: `Invalid input for tool \"${name}\"`};\n    }\n    log.info('tool', 'executing', {name, inputKeys: Object.keys(input)});","old_string":"    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n    if (!tool) {\n      log.warn('tool', 'tool not found', {name});\n      throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}`);\n    }\n    if (tool.validator && !tool.validator(input)) {\n      log.warn('tool', 'input validation failed', {name});\n      return {result: `Invalid input for tool \"${name}\"`};\n    }\n    log.info('tool', 'executing', {name, inputKeys: Object.keys(input)});","file_path":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/9f6517f7108d/workspace/target/src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts","instruction":"Resolve and WeakMap-cache validators for function-valued ToolDefinitionSource schemas in ToolRegistry.execute."}}
{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":"2026-11-15T16:09:18.761Z","tool_name":"replace","tool_id":"replace__call_411725369257196792","parameters":{"old_string":"const ajv = new ajvPackage.default({strict: false, validateFormats: false});\n\nfunction compileToolSchema(definition: ToolDefinition): ValidateFunction {","new_string":"const dynamicValidators = new WeakMap<Record<string, unknown>, ValidateFunction>();\n\nfunction resolveDynamicValidator(definition: ToolDefinition): ValidateFunction {\n  const cached = dynamicValidators.get(definition.inputSchema);\n  if (cached) return cached;\n  const compiled = compileToolSchema(definition);\n  dynamicValidators.set(definition.inputSchema, compiled);\n  return compiled;\n}\n\nconst AjvConstructor = ajvPackage.default;\nconst ajv = new AjvConstructor({strict: false, validateFormats: false});\n\nfunction compileToolSchema(definition: ToolDefinition): ValidateFunction {","file_path":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/9f6517f7108d/workspace/target/src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts","instruction":"Add resolveDynamicValidator backed by a WeakMap keyed by inputSchema object reference above compileToolSchema."}}
